leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, release the follower, and on 5-6-7 step toward the center/next partner while jumping or reaching up to clap once overhead ('un fly').
Step on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) while clapping overhead a second time ('dos fly') as you arrive at the new follower, then lead her through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Turn left in the Enchufla on 1-2-3, then mark basic steps in place along the circle on 5-6-7 while clapping overhead once ('un fly') with the group.
Mark in place on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) with the second overhead clap ('dos fly'), connect with the incoming leader on count 12, and execute Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Safety: If adding a small hop on the 'fly' catch, land softly on the balls of the feet with bent knees and check vertical clearance so raised elbows do not strike a partner.
Clapping in front of the chest like a regular Dame con una instead of reaching high overhead as if catching a baseball.
Being late to connect on count 12 for the Dile Que No exit.
variations: Un fly (single overhead catch in 1 eight-count: Enchufla on 1-3, catch on 4/5, Dile Que No on 5-7).
Tres fly (extending the sequence for an extra count).
notes: Named after catching a fly ball in Cuban baseball ('un fly'). Ensure dancers keep the overhead clap crisp so they are ready to connect on count 12.

name: Dos Tarros
summary: A dynamic Rueda partner-change call where leaders advance two partners counter-clockwise by performing two consecutive 'Tarro' (bull-horn/underarm) transitions without pausing for Dile Que No in between.

leaderSteps.text: On 1-2-3, step forward and raise the left arm to turn the current follower as you duck or pass underneath toward the next partner ('un tarro'); on 5-6-7, immediately catch the next follower and repeat the pass toward the second follower ('dos tarros').
Connect with the second new follower on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) to stabilize in closed hold, then lead her cleanly through a Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Step and turn in place along the outside of the circle on 1-2-3 as the first leader passes through, then repeat the turn/frame connection on 5-6-7 as the next leader passes.
Connect in closed frame on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) with the arriving leader and travel through a standard Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Safety: Leaders bending at the waist with the head down during the duck-under instead of bending at the knees and keeping the spine upright to avoid elbow collisions.
Stopping to do a Dile Que No with the first follower instead of flowing directly to the second partner.
Followers wandering inward off the circle perimeter, blocking the leaders' travelling lane.
variations: Tarro de mentira (faking the second pass and returning to the first partner).
notes: Safety note: Ensure leaders keep their free hand up as a guard and bend their knees rather than hinging their neck forward when ducking under the arm.

name: Echeverría
summary: A classic Rueda call where an Enchufla entry is followed by a rhythmic pause/step-tap in the center before the leader travels to the next partner into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3, trading places with your follower.
Step toward the center of the Rueda on 5-6-7 with the signature Echeverría check/tap (or feint toward the current partner before moving on).
Travel to the next follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Hold the outer circle with a rhythmic basic check on 5-6-7.
Connect with the incoming leader on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Moving to the next partner on count 5 instead of executing the middle check.
Losing the circular shape of the Rueda during the center check.
variations: Adding a vocal shout or clap on the count 7 break.
notes: UNSURE: 'Echeverría' varies between Cuban and European Rueda traditions (sometimes taught as a fake Dame / Engáñala, sometimes as an Enchufla with a footwork tap). Verify with Enrique.

name: Echeverría con Vuelta
summary: An extended variation of the Echeverría Rueda call combining an Enchufla, a rhythmic foot-tap/clap break with a solo 360-degree turn ('con vuelta'), and a partner change into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 to face the center of the Rueda, then perform the signature Echeverría syncopated step-tap/clap pattern on 5-6-7.
Execute a crisp solo 360-degree turn on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) while travelling to the next follower on the right, and lead her through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3, then mirror the rhythmic Echeverría step-tap/clap break in place on 5-6-7.
Execute a solo 360-degree turn in place on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), connect with the incoming leader on count 12, and travel through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Spinning too fast on counts 9-11 and losing sight of the new partner before the Dile Que No connection on count 12.
Forgetting to advance to the next partner during the solo turn.
Rushing the rhythmic break on 5-6-7.
variations: Adding a vocal chant during the 5-6-7 break before the turn.
notes: UNSURE: 'Echeverría' choreography varies between Cuban and European Rueda lineages (some do side-chassé claps, others do a backward kick-hitch before the turn). Teacher should verify the exact counts 5-7 footwork used in class.

name: Egoísta
summary: The 'Selfish Leader': the leader starts an Enchufla as if giving the follower to the next leader, then 'selfishly' pulls back/hooks his own follower around himself on 5-7 to keep her for Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, keeping a light hook connection instead of releasing on count 3.
Instead of moving to the next partner, draw your original follower back around your right side into a protective 'selfish' embrace on 5-6-7.
Open the frame on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No with your original follower on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the Enchufla on 1-2-3 while maintaining your connected hand.
Follow the leader's continuous inward lead on 5-6-7 to curve back around into his closed embrace.
Step back on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Yanking the follower's arm on count 4/5 to pull her back; use continuous circular body rotation.
Releasing the hand on count 3 out of Enchufla habit.
variations: Egoísta con Vuelta (adding an inside turn as you bring the follower back).
notes: Does NOT change partner—the leader 'selfishly' keeps his own partner!

name: El Dedo con Guarapo y Bota
spanishName: El dedo con guarapo y bota
summary: A signature advanced Rueda combination that chains 'El Dedo' (right-to-right index/hook turn and leader duck-under) with 'Guarapo' (sweet circular wrap/grind) and 'Bota' (throwing/releasing the partner to the next station) into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Execute El Dedo: from a right-to-right hold, turn the follower on 1-3 and duck under the raised right arm on 5-7.
Flow directly into Guarapo on 1-3 and 5-7 (wrapping into a close, circular sugarcane-press groove with the follower).
Execute 'y Bota' on 1-3 (unwinding and releasing/sending the follower outward) while advancing to the next follower on 5-7.
Collect the new follower on 1-3 and finish with Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Follow the right-to-right El Dedo turn on 1-3 and walk around the leader on 5-7 as he ducks under.
Match the circular 'Guarapo' wrap and Cuban hip/torso groove on 1-3 and 5-7.
Spin cleanly out on the 'Bota' release on 1-3 and hold your perimeter station on 5-7.
Connect with the incoming leader on 1-3 and walk through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Never literally 'lock' a single index finger on El Dedo—use a safe two-finger palm hook so no finger joint can be sprained.
SAFETY: Ducking with a bent neck on count 5 instead of lowering with the knees.
variations: El Dedo con Guarapo (staying with the same partner without 'Bota').
notes: Directly extends the 'dedo-el-uno-el-dos' curriculum module into a full Rueda showpiece.

name: El Puente
summary: The 'Bridge': from a two-hand hold (or Enchufla pickup), the couple raises both arms to form an overhead bridge on 1-3 while the leader (or follower) ducks underneath on 5-7 before resolving into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: From a two-hand connection, lead an opening turn/prep on 1-2-3 and raise both joined hands high to form a bridge arch.
Duck smoothly underneath the two-hand bridge on 5-6-7 by bending your knees while guiding the follower around.
Unwind the arms overhead on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No (with your current or next partner) on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step 1-2-3 while keeping both elbows soft and hands raised in the bridge arch.
Walk around the leader on 5-6-7 as he passes underneath the bridge, maintaining a loose finger hook.
Step back on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Pulling down on the follower's wrists while ducking under the bridge; lower with your legs and keep your spine upright.
Clamping thumbs during the wrist rotation under the bridge.
variations: El Puente con Dame (releasing after the bridge to take the next follower).
notes: Confirm whether BOH Studios uses 'El Puente' as a partner-change Rueda call or stays with the same partner.

name: Enchufla con Mambo
summary: A high-energy Rueda call where the leader and follower execute an Enchufla on 1-3, face the center for a synchronized Mambo forward-and-back shine on counts 5-11, and switch partners into Dile Que No on 13-15.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a clean Enchufla on 1-2-3, releasing hands on count 3 after trading places.
Face the center (or your partner) and dance a grounded Mambo shine step on 5-6-7 with Cuban ribcage and arm groove.
Finish the Mambo step on 9-11 while rotating toward the next follower on your right, then lead Dile Que No with the new partner on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3 and release connection.
Dance the Mambo shine step in place on 5-6-7, adding hip and shoulder styling.
Complete the Mambo step on 9-11, connect with the incoming leader on 12, and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Switching partners immediately on count 5 and skipping the Mambo shine.
Doing the Mambo shine with stiff knees and zero upper-body groove.
Forgetting to move to the new partner on count 11/12.
variations: Enchufla con Mambo Sexy (adding a playful body roll on 5-7).
notes: Check with BOH Studios teachers whether the Mambo section lasts 1 slow four-count (5-6-7) before Dile Que No on the next 1-3, or a full 8-count.

name: Enchufla con Manolín
summary: Named after Cuban Timba icon Manolín 'El Médico de la Salsa': an Enchufla on 1-3 followed by Manolín's signature overhead/pumping hand gesture and rhythmic step on 5-7 before switching partners into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3 and release connection.
Step toward the center/next follower on 5-6-7 while performing the signature 'Manolín' arm pump / overhead party gesture to the beat.
Pick up the next follower on 9-11 and finish with Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Hold your perimeter spot on 5-6-7 while joining in the playful Manolín arm/body groove.
Connect with the incoming leader on 9-11 and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Doing the arm gesture stiffly without grounded Cuban knee and hip action.
Forgetting to advance to the next partner by count 9.
variations: Shouting '¡Arriba de la bola!' (Manolín's famous catchphrase) on counts 5-7.
notes: UNSURE: Different schools use slightly different hand gestures for 'Manolín' (rolling fists overhead vs pumping one hand). Teacher should confirm BOH Studios' gesture.

name: Enchufla con Palma y Pata'
summary: A percussive Rueda partner-change call where an Enchufla on 1-3 is followed by a synchronized clap ('palma') and playful foot kick/stamp ('patá') on counts 5-7 before picking up the next follower in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3 and release connection.
Face the center on 5-6-7, executing the rhythmic clap ('palma') and a low, controlled foot kick/stomp ('patá') while shifting toward the next follower.
Collect the new follower on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Match the rhythmic clap ('palma') and low kick/stomp ('patá') on 5-6-7 from your spot on the outer perimeter.
Connect with the incoming leader on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Kicking high or forward toward the center of the circle and striking another dancer's shin; keep the 'patá' low and compact under your own body.
Losing balance on the standing leg during the kick and arriving late on count 9.
variations: Doubling the clap-and-kick rhythm over an extra eight-count.
notes: 'Patá' is the Cuban coastal contraction of 'patada' (kick/stomp). Emphasize low, safe footwork in crowded circles.

name: Enchufla con Rumba
summary: A flavour-packed Rueda call where an Enchufla on 1-3 opens into a 4-count (or 12-count) Rumba Guaguancó groove with shoulder isolations and vacunao play before switching partners into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a clean Enchufla on 1-2-3 and release hands.
Drop into a grounded Rumba Guaguancó stance on 5-6-7, executing lateral Guaguancó steps, shoulder rolls, and a playful vacunao gesture toward your current or next follower.
Transition to the next follower on 9-11 and finish with Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Answer with authentic Rumba Guaguancó hip motion, torso isolation, and a protective vacunao skirt/hand cover on 5-6-7.
Connect with the incoming leader on 9-11 and travel cleanly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Dancing a stiff basic step on 5-7 instead of softening the knees and isolating the ribcage for Rumba.
Forgetting to move to the new partner on count 9.
variations: Extending the Rumba Guaguancó breakdown for an extra full eight-count when the music drops into a rumba section.
notes: Confirm whether BOH Studios dances the Rumba break for 4 counts (5-6-7) or 12 counts (5-7 + 1-7) before Dile Que No.

name: Enchufla con Vuelta
summary: An Enchufla variation where, after the initial 1-3 exchange, the leader (or both dancers) executes a solo 360-degree turn ('vuelta') in the center on counts 5-7 before picking up the next follower in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a clean Enchufla on 1-2-3 and release connection on count 3.
Execute a crisp solo 360-degree turn (left or right, per house call) on 5-6-7 while traveling along the inside lane toward the next follower.
Connect with the new follower on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Step in place on the outer circle on 5-6-7 (or execute a matching solo turn if called for both) while spotting the incoming leader.
Step back on 9-11 and walk cleanly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Spinning blindly on 5-6-7 without spotting the next follower, leading to dizziness or collisions.
Turning so slowly that you miss the count 9 pickup.
variations: Enchufla con Doble Vuelta (fast double spin on 5-6-7).
notes: Clarify with students whether only the leader turns on 5-7 or both leader and follower execute the solo vuelta.

name: Enchufla Contra-Mambo
summary: An Enchufla entry on 1-3 that immediately locks into a syncopated Contra-Mambo check on 5-7 before switching partners into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a crisp Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Instead of a standard Mambo basic, hit the syncopated Contra-Mambo rhythm/direction check on 5-6-7 while transitioning toward the next follower.
Connect with the new follower on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Hit the syncopated Contra-Mambo check on 5-6-7 on the outer circle.
Step back on 9-11 and walk cleanly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Drifting off clave during the syncopated 5-7 Contra-Mambo break.
Arriving late to the next partner on count 9.
variations: Extending the Contra-Mambo for an extra 8-count.
notes: Pairs with 'Contra Mambo' from Batch 9.

name: Enchufla Contra-Mambo Doble
summary: A syncopated Rueda call where couples execute an Enchufla on counts 1-3, perform two consecutive rounds of contratiempo/syncopated mambo footwork checks ('contra-mambo doble') facing the center, and change partners into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 to swap places and face the center, then execute the first syncopated contra-mambo footwork break on 5-6-7.
Repeat the contra-mambo footwork break with opposite/alternating directional checks on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and 5-6-7 (counts 13-15) for the 'doble' extension.
On counts 17-24, travel counter-clockwise to the next follower on 1-2-3 and lead her cleanly through Dile Que No on 5-6-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn left in the opening Enchufla on 1-2-3, then execute the first syncopated contra-mambo footwork break in place on 5-6-7.
Perform the second round of contra-mambo footwork on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and 5-6-7 (counts 13-15) with sharp ribcage contrapunto.
On counts 17-24, connect with the incoming leader on 1-2-3 and travel through Dile Que No on 5-6-7.

commonMistakes: Drifting back onto standard 1-3-5-7 flat mambo taps instead of hitting the contratiempo/syncopated 'contra-mambo' accents.
Exiting to the new partner after the first mambo break instead of completing the 'doble'.
Looking at the floor during the footwork and losing awareness of the circle.
variations: Maintaining single-hand connection with the partner during the contra-mambo checks.
notes: UNSURE: Confirm whether 'Contra-Mambo' in your syllabus is danced solo facing the center or in partner check hold (pushing/checking against each other's frame in contrapunto).

name: Enchufla Moderno
summary: A sleek, contemporary Rueda variation of Enchufla that adds a behind-the-back hand change, a syncopated check, or an extra inside turn on counts 5-7 before advancing to the next follower for Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 while switching the connection behind your back (or leading a double/checked turn).
Guide the follower through the secondary modern check/turn on 5-6-7 while stepping into the inside lane toward the next partner.
Collect the next follower on 9-11 and finish with Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3 with an active core.
Follow the secondary turn or syncopated check on 5-6-7 along the outer perimeter.
Connect with the incoming leader on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Yanking the behind-the-back hand switch when standing too far apart.
Rushing the secondary turn on 5-7 and arriving off-balance on count 9.
variations: Enchufla Moderno con Alarde.
notes: UNSURE: Different instructors teach slightly different hand switches for 'Enchufla Moderno'. Teacher should verify BOH Studios' exact sequence.

name: Enchufla para Hombres
summary: A role-reversed Enchufla where the follower holds the framing station on 1-3 while the leader executes the traveling inside underarm turn, followed by a partner switch into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Raise the connected left-to-right arm on 1 and execute the traveling underarm turn yourself on 1-2-3 while trading places with the follower.
Step along the inside lane on 5-6-7 toward the next follower.
Collect the new follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step back/side on 1-2-3 to trade places around the circle while framing the raised arm for the leader's underarm turn.
Settle onto the outer perimeter on 5-6-7 and spot the incoming leader.
Step back on 9-11 and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Followers pulling the leader's arm down while he turns underneath; keep the raised window high and relaxed.
Followers turning on 1-3 out of Enchufla muscle memory when 'para hombres' was called.
variations: Enchufla para Hombres Doble.
notes: Tests whether followers are truly listening to the caller rather than turning automatically on every 'Enchufla...' call.

name: Enchufla y Adiós
summary: A seamless 2-bar combination that chains an Enchufla on 1-3 directly into an Adiós (Prima) underarm pass on 5-7 (or 9-11) before resolving with the next follower in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3, exchanging places with your follower.
Instead of stepping into Dile Que No, use the 5-6-7 counts to cross in front and duck under your raised arm in an Adiós (Prima) pass while advancing to the next follower.
Connect with the new follower on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Frame the Adiós (Prima) pass on 5-6-7 as the leader crosses and ducks under the raised arm.
Receive the incoming leader on 9-11 and travel cleanly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Ducking under the Adiós arm by bending the neck instead of lowering with the knees.
Forgetting that 'Adiós' is the classic Havana name for 'Prima'.
variations: Enchufla y Adiós con la Hermana (3 eight-counts).
notes: Reinforces the connection between the two most important foundational moves in Rueda: Enchufla and Prima (Adiós).

name: Enchufla y al Medio
summary: A Rueda call where leaders execute an Enchufla on counts 1-3, bring the action or rhythmic footwork tightly into the center of the circle ('al medio') on 5-7, and transition to the next partner in Dile Que No on the second eight-count.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 to swap places, then step forward into the tight center ring ('al medio') on 5-6-7 to perform the center footwork/clap accent with the other leaders.
Step back out of the center on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) toward the next follower on the right, and lead her cleanly through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Turn left in the Enchufla on 1-2-3, then mark Cuban basic in place along the outer perimeter (or step slightly inward if all dancers go 'al medio') on 5-6-7.
Step back-side-together on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) as the new leader steps out from the center to connect, and travel through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Leaders staying too deep in the center on count 11 and having to lunge to reach the new follower for Dile Que No.
Followers drifting inward while the leaders are in the middle, leaving no space for the Dile Que No slot.
Losing the basic timing while improvising in the center.
variations: Holding the center groove across multiple eight-counts if followed by 'Síguelo'.
notes: Level note: Rueda.Casino lists it as Advanced, though the mechanics are accessible to Improver/Intermediate dancers; in an Advanced class, emphasize tight musical syncopation in the center and razor-sharp spacing.

name: Enchufla y Cadeneta
summary: A Rueda call starting with an Enchufla on 1-3 that transitions immediately into a continuous linked-arm or alternating-hand chain ('cadeneta') around the circle, ending with a partner change in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 with the current follower, then on 5-6-7 hook or connect with the next follower in line to initiate the alternating Cadeneta weave.
Continue weaving counter-clockwise through the Cadeneta on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and 5-6-7 (counts 13-15), exchanging places with each passing follower.
On counts 17-24, collect the designated follower on 1-2-3 and lead her through a Dile Que No on 5-6-7 to re-form the circle.

followerSteps.text: Turn left in the opening Enchufla on 1-2-3, then on 5-6-7 connect with the next leader to begin travelling clockwise through the Cadeneta chain.
Weave smoothly from leader to leader on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and 5-6-7 (counts 13-15), keeping the arm connection light and responsive.
On counts 17-24, connect in closed frame on 1-2-3 with the final leader and travel through Dile Que No on 5-6-7.

commonMistakes: Safety: Hooking elbows rigidly during the Cadeneta weave—use hands or soft forearm contact so no one's shoulder is pulled if a dancer steps off time.
Breaking the circular shape of the Rueda by cutting across the middle.
Rushing the weave steps instead of stepping strictly on 1-2-3 and 5-6-7.
variations: Continuing the Cadeneta indefinitely until the caller shouts 'Dile Que No'.
notes: UNSURE: Confirm how many partners are passed in the fixed-length version of 'Enchufla y Cadeneta' before the Dile Que No exit.

name: Enchufla y Escóndete
summary: 'Enchufla and Hide!': after an Enchufla on 1-3, the leader steps behind the next follower on 5-7 to 'hide' behind her back before emerging on 9-11 to lead Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3 and release connection.
Travel quickly to the next follower on your right and step behind her back on 5-6-7 ('hiding' on the outside of the circle), peeking playfully over her shoulder.
Step around to the inside/front of that follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Hold your spot on the circle on 5-6-7 without stepping backward so the incoming leader has safe space to 'hide' behind you.
Connect with the leader as he steps around to your front on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Followers taking a large back-step on count 5 and stepping onto the toes of the leader hiding behind them!
Leaders grabbing the follower's shoulders from behind and startling her.
variations: Tapping the follower lightly on the opposite shoulder from behind as a playful decoy on count 7.
notes: Crucial safety cue for followers: on 'Escóndete', keep your 5-6-7 steps directly underneath your hips, never back.

name: Enchufla y Quédate
summary: A Rueda call where the couple executes an Enchufla on counts 1-3, the leader cancels the usual partner change after the call '¡Quédate!', and keeps the same partner by finishing with Dile Que No in place on 5-7.

leaderSteps.text: Step back-side-together on 1-2-3, raising the left arm to lead the follower into an inside left turn while exchanging places with her. Pause on 4.
Instead of releasing and moving to the next partner in the circle, stay with the current follower, connect in closed hold on 4, and lead her through a Dile Que No on 5-6-7. Pause on 8.

followerSteps.text: Step forward and turn left under the leader's raised left arm on 1-2-3 to swap places, facing the leader by count 3. Pause on 4.
Remain with the same leader, allowing him to connect on the back/shoulder on 4, and walk through the Dile Que No arc on 5-6-7 to return to Guapea. Pause on 8.

commonMistakes: Leaders running off toward the next woman on count 4 out of habit before hearing the 'y quédate' modifier.
Followers turning away toward the outside of the circle on count 4 expecting a partner change instead of keeping eyes on their current leader.
Taking two full eight-counts by adding an extra basic in the middle instead of flowing directly into Dile Que No on 5-6-7.
variations: Enchufla y Quédate en Cerrado (finishing in closed hold on 5-7 ready for Prima or Sacala instead of Dile Que No).
notes: In standard Rueda, a bare 'Enchufla' implies a partner change ('Enchufla y Dame'). 'Enchufla y Quédate' tests whether dancers are truly listening to the cantante rather than running on autopilot.

name: Enchufla y Rodeo
summary: An intermediate Rueda combination where an Enchufla on 1-3 transitions directly into a circular Rodeo wrap/orbit around the follower before releasing to the next partner into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-3, then on 5-7 catch or guide the follower into a circular Rodeo orbit around your right side.
Complete the 360-degree Rodeo rotation on 1-3 and unwrap/release on 5-7 as you step toward the next follower.
Collect the new follower on 1-3 and finish with Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-3 and curve smoothly into the Rodeo orbit on 5-7.
Walk around the shared Rodeo axis on 1-3 and unwind onto the outer perimeter on 5-7.
Connect with the incoming leader on 1-3 and walk through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Pulling the follower's arm behind her back during the Rodeo orbit; keep the framing arm soft around the waist/shoulder blades.
Making the Rodeo circle too wide and colliding with neighbouring couples.
variations: 2-bar compact Enchufla y Rodeo.
notes: Maps directly to the canonical 'Rodeo' enum value in the Rueda call list.

name: Enchúflense
summary: A mutual/double Enchufla where both leader and follower turn simultaneously while trading places, or where an Enchufla is immediately mirrored before switching partners into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Initiate an Enchufla on 1-2-3 while simultaneously executing an inward/underarm turn alongside the follower as you trade places.
Complete the mutual exchange on 5-6-7, advancing along the inside of the circle toward the next follower.
Connect with the new follower on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3 while keeping your elbow soft as the leader also turns.
Settle onto the outer perimeter on 5-6-7 and spot the incoming leader.
Step back on 9-11 and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Pulling on the joined hand while both dancers are turning simultaneously; use a light touch or release at the apex of the turn.
Over-rotating and losing orientation in the circle.
variations: Performing Enchúflense completely hands-free (Suelta style) on 1-3.
notes: UNSURE: Check if BOH Studios teaches 'Enchúflense' as a simultaneous double-turn on 1-3 or as leader-turns-then-follower-turns.

name: Engáñala
summary: 'Trick Her / Fake Her Out!': the leader starts an Enchufla or Dame as if moving to the next partner on the right, fakes the step on 5-6, and returns to their original follower on 9-15 for Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3, trading places with your current follower.
Step toward the next follower on your right on 5-6 as if switching partners, then check your weight and pivot back toward your original follower on 7.
Reconnect with your original follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Dance your basic in place on 5-6-7, watching the leader's playful decoy step and staying ready for his return.
Receive your original leader on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Committing your full body weight to the next follower and failing to pivot back by count 9.
SAFETY: Backing up into the neighbouring leader during the feint.
variations: Engáñala con las Manos (faking a right-hand lead and switching to the left hand).
notes: Closely related to '¡Mentira!', except 'Engáñala' is called upfront before the figure starts, whereas '¡Mentira!' is shouted mid-move as a surprise cancellation.

name: Enróscala
summary: 'Coil Her Up!': the leader guides the follower into a waist-level spiral wrap ('enróscala') on 1-3 and uncoils her with a crisp reverse spin on 5-7 before resolving into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: From a two-hand or left-to-right hold, lead the follower to turn inward on 1-2-3 so her connected arm wraps smoothly around her own waist.
Gently lead the uncoiling spin in the opposite direction on 5-6-7, letting her unwind like a spring.
Collect the follower (or next follower, if called with Dame) on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn into the waist-level coil wrap on 1-2-3, keeping your forearm resting lightly against your own abdomen/waist.
Use the gentle waist-level lead on 5-6-7 to uncoil and spin cleanly on your own vertical axis.
Step back on 9-11 and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Yanking the waist-wrapped hand forcefully on count 5, which spins the follower off her axis; use a progressive, cushioned lead.
Raising the wrapped hand up to chest or neck height instead of keeping it at the waist.
variations: Enróscala y Dame (switching partners as the follower uncoils).
notes: Confirm whether BOH Studios changes partners on 'Enróscala' by default or stays with the same partner.

name: Enróscate
summary: The leader coils ('enrosca') into a self-wrap or spiral turn while keeping connection with the follower, then uncoils cleanly into an Enchufla or Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: From open hold, step 1-2-3 while turning inward to wrap the connected arm around your own waist or back ('coiling in').
Uncoil with a reverse pivot on 5-6-7, using the stored rotational momentum to lead the follower across.
Complete the place exchange on 9-11 and resolve with Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step Guapea or compact circular walks on 1-2-3 while giving the leader space to coil into their wrap.
Keep a light, steady frame at waist level as the leader uncoils on 5-6-7.
Step back on 9-11 and travel smoothly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Wrapping the arm tightly around the elbow or yanking the follower forward while coiling.
Losing balance during the leader's spiral turn.
Forgetting to step on 1-2-3 while coiling.
variations: Leading a double spiral (Enrosca) on the spot when dancing on a crowded social floor.
notes: Great for teaching leaders how to turn on their own axis without pulling on the follower's frame.

name: Espresso
summary: A fast-paced Rueda partner-change call where leaders weave rapidly past multiple followers (like an express train) along the circle before settling into Dile Que No with a new partner.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an opening Enchufla on 1-2-3, then accelerate counter-clockwise along the inside of the circle on 5-6-7, passing the first available follower with a quick hand tap or check.
Continue to the next follower down the line on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), connect in closed frame, and decelerate smoothly into a Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Turn left in the opening Enchufla on 1-2-3, then travel clockwise (or mark along the outer perimeter) on 5-6-7 while offering a light hand check to the passing leader.
Connect with the arriving leader on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and complete a grounded Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Yanking the intermediate follower's arm while jogging past at high speed.
Failing to decelerate on counts 9-11, causing the final Dile Que No to swing wide out of the circle.
Losing the 1-2-3, 5-6-7 pulse during the fast travel.
variations: Doble Espresso (continuing the fast weave for an additional eight-count).
notes: UNSURE: 'Espresso' (or 'Expreso') varies by Rueda lineage—some use it as a rapid multi-partner weave, others as a compact fast Coca-Cola/Enchufla combo. Teacher should confirm the exact choreography.

name: Esquina de Tejas
summary: Named after the famous Havana corner/intersection in El Cerro: a multi-directional advanced combination featuring sharp 90- and 180-degree directional checks, wraps, and intricate arm knots.

leaderSteps.text: Enter with a two-hand knot (Setenta/Sombrero base) on 1-3 and lead a sharp corner check ('esquina') on 5-7.
Redirect the follower along a perpendicular circular arc on 1-3 and duck/turn under the joined arms on 5-7.
Unwind the double arm wrap sequentially on 1-3 and 5-7 while maintaining close proximity.
Collect the frame on 1-3 and close with a dynamic Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn into the initial wrap on 1-3 and absorb the corner check cleanly with your core and lats on 5-7.
Pivot onto the new circular path on 1-3 and step compactly on 5-7 while the leader turns through the window.
Follow the sequential overhead unwraps on 1-3 and 5-7 with self-supported balance.
Step back on 1-3 and complete Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Leading the sharp 'corner' direction checks with rigid wrists instead of a cushioned frame check.
SAFETY: Ducking under the arm knot with a bent neck; lower with the knees.
Rushing the 4-eight-count phrasing.
variations: Shortening to 3 eight-counts for faster Timba montunos.
notes: UNSURE: Named after Havana's historic Esquina de Tejas; exact choreography varies between Havana instructors. Teacher must verify the BOH Studios sequence.

name: Estrella (Se Fue)
summary: The 'Star': all leaders (or all dancers) join hands in the exact center of the Rueda to form a rotating star wheel while the outer ring circles, releasing into a partner pickup and Dile Que No when the caller shouts '¡Se fue!'.

leaderSteps.text: After an Enchufla on 1-3, step into the center on 5-7 and place your right (or left) hand into the central hub with all other leaders to form the 'Estrella' star.
Walk around the center hub in the star formation on 1-3 and 5-7 while the followers circle/groove on the outside.
When the caller shouts '¡Se fue!', release the star on 1, pick up the nearest outer follower on 2-3, and lead Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla turn on 1-3 and stay on the outer perimeter on 5-7.
Walk or groove rhythmically around the outer perimeter on 1-3 and 5-7 while the leaders rotate the inner star.
On '¡Se fue!', connect with the emerging leader on 1-3 and walk cleanly through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Pressing down on the stacked hands in the center star hub.
Scrambling across the circle on '¡Se fue!' instead of smoothly taking the follower directly beside you.
variations: Estrella de Mujeres (followers form the center star while leaders walk the perimeter).
notes: The caller can keep the Estrella rotating for as many bars as the musical section lasts before calling '¡Se fue!' or '¡Dile que no!'.

name: Exhíbela > Repite
summary: A continuous Rueda drill where the leader leads an Exhíbela (Sácala) clockwise turn for the follower on 1-7 and immediately repeats a second Exhíbela on 9-15 when the caller shouts '¡Repite!' or '¡Otra!'.

leaderSteps.text: From closed hold or Dile Que No pickup, step back/open on 1-3 and lead the follower through a clean clockwise Exhíbela turn under your raised right arm on 5-7.
Instead of closing into Guapea, absorb the follower's momentum on 9-11 with your right hand on her back and lead a second consecutive Exhíbela turn on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step forward on 1-3 to open out and execute a smooth clockwise turn under the leader's raised right arm on 5-6-7.
Feel the leader's back-frame check on 9-11 (without dropping into Guapea) and flow straight into a second clockwise Exhíbela turn on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Switching to a rock-back Guapea on count 9 when the leader is leading a second Exhíbela.
Cranking the follower's arm overhead instead of guiding from her shoulder blade on 9-11.
Followers losing their vertical axis on the second consecutive turn.
variations: Exhíbela Tres Veces (repeating three times in a row).
notes: Essential beginner drill for teaching followers to wait for the leader's frame on count 1 rather than assuming every Exhíbela ends in Guapea.

name: Familia y Quédate
summary: A Rueda call starting like 'Prima con la Familia' (an Enchufla/Prima entry toward the center of the circle to greet the group), but instead of advancing to the next partner, the leader stays ('y quédate') with his original follower and finishes with Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead the opening Prima/Enchufla check on 1-2-3 and bring the follower inward to face the center of the circle with the group on 5-6-7.
Instead of releasing and moving to the next partner as in standard Familia, keep hold of your own follower on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and lead her through a Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Step through the opening Prima/Enchufla check on 1-2-3 and pivot to join the inner ring on 5-6-7.
Stay connected to the same leader on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) rather than looking for the incoming leader, and travel through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Leaders automatically releasing their partner on count 8 to change partners because they didn't process 'y quédate'.
Followers turning away toward the previous leader expecting a partner change.
Collapsing the circle too tightly in the center on counts 5-7.
variations: Adding a group clap or vocal greeting in the center on count 8 before returning to the same partner.
notes: UNSURE: In some schools 'Familia' is an Enchufla into a group hands-in-the-middle greeting, while in others it is 'Prima con la hermana/familia'. Confirm the exact first eight-count entry.

name: Festival de Enchufla Complicado
summary: A multi-part Rueda sequence chaining three distinct Enchufla variations (such as Enchufla Doble, Enchufla con Alarde/Vuelta, and Enchufla con Mambo/Claps) with partner changes across the sequence.

leaderSteps.text: Execute part one: lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 and check the follower back to her place on 5-6-7 (Enchufla Doble initiation).
Complete the third Enchufla swap on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), advance to the next follower, and lead Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).
On counts 17-24, execute part two with the new partner: Enchufla on 1-2-3 followed by a leader hook-turn or Ronde/Alarde on 5-6-7.
Advance to the second new partner on 1-2-3 (counts 25-27) and lead Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 29-31).
On counts 33-40, execute part three: Enchufla on 1-2-3 with a double-hand wrap or syncopated footwork break on 5-6-7.
Advance to the third partner on 1-2-3 (counts 41-43) and close the festival with Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 45-47).

followerSteps.text: Execute part one: turn left in the Enchufla on 1-2-3 and check back in the reverse turn on 5-6-7.
Turn left again on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), receive the incoming leader, and dance Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).
On counts 17-24, execute the second Enchufla variation on 1-2-3 and 5-6-7 with the new leader.
Receive the second incoming leader on 1-2-3 (counts 25-27) and dance Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 29-31).
On counts 33-40, execute the third Enchufla variation on 1-2-3 and 5-6-7.
Receive the final incoming leader on 1-2-3 (counts 41-43) and finish with Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 45-47).

commonMistakes: Safety: If the complication includes a neck wrap or hammerlock, keep tension light and release the lower hand before leading the partner change.
Mixing up the order of the three Enchufla variations.
Falling behind the music during the transitions between sections.
variations: Changing partners only at the very end of the festival rather than after each of the three parts.
notes: UNSURE: Every Rueda school defines the 3 sub-parts of 'Festival de Enchufla Complicado' slightly differently. Teacher must check and edit the three specific Enchufla variations to match the Bournemouth syllabus.

name: Festival de Fly (Los Tres)
summary: A high-energy baseball-themed Rueda sequence that chains three distinct 'Fly' variations (such as Un Fly, Dos Fly, and Tres Fly—or Fly arriba, al medio, y abajo) before finishing with a partner change into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead the first Enchufla on 1-3 and execute the first overhead 'Fly' clap on 5-7.
Lead the second Enchufla on 1-3 and execute the second Fly variation (double overhead clap or mid-level catch) on 5-7.
Lead the third Enchufla on 1-3 and execute the third Fly variation on 5-7 while advancing to the next follower.
Collect the new follower on 1-3 and complete Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the first Enchufla on 1-3 and hit the first overhead Fly clap on 5-7.
Turn through the second Enchufla on 1-3 and hit the second Fly clap variation on 5-7.
Turn through the third Enchufla on 1-3 and hit the third Fly variation on 5-7 on the perimeter.
Connect with the incoming leader on 1-3 and walk through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Swinging arms wide during the overhead claps and bumping neighbouring dancers.
Confusing 'Festival de Fly' with 'Festival de Pelota'.
variations: Switching partners after each of the three Flys (6 eight-counts total).
notes: UNSURE: Confirm whether BOH Studios switches partners after each of the 3 Flys or only at the end of the third Fly.

name: Festival de Media
summary: A fast-paced Rueda festival sequence chaining multiple 'Media' (half-Enchufla / half-turn direction-reversal) variations in succession with partner changes across the circle.

leaderSteps.text: Execute part one: lead a 'Media' check on 1-2-3 (stopping the Enchufla halfway so both partners rebound), then complete the swap and advance to the next partner on 5-6-7.
Lead the first new partner through Dile Que No on counts 9-16 (or transition directly into part two).
On counts 17-24, execute part two ('Media Doble'): two half-checks on 1-2-3 and 5-6-7 before completing the Enchufla pass.
Advance to the second new partner and lead Dile Que No on counts 25-32.
On counts 33-40, execute part three ('Media Complicada / con Vuelta'): half-check on 1-2-3 followed by a full turn and pass on 5-6-7.
Advance to the third partner on 1-2-3 (counts 41-43) and finish the festival with Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 45-47).

followerSteps.text: Execute part one: step into the half-Enchufla check on 1-2-3, rebound cleanly from the core, and complete the turn on 5-6-7.
Dance Dile Que No with the first incoming leader on counts 9-16.
On counts 17-24, execute the double half-check on 1-2-3 and 5-6-7.
Complete the pass and dance Dile Que No with the second incoming leader on counts 25-32.
On counts 33-40, execute the third Media variation with a crisp turn on 5-6-7.
Connect with the final incoming leader on 1-2-3 (counts 41-43) and finish with Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 45-47).

commonMistakes: Safety: Never yank the follower's arm to create the 'Media' half-check—use a flat palm-to-palm or forearm frame check at chest level.
Followers completing the full Enchufla turn on counts 1-3 instead of feeling the midway check.
Losing track of which of the three festival parts is currently active.
variations: Running all three Media variations back-to-back with a single Dile Que No at the very end.
notes: UNSURE: 'Festival de Media' (or 'Festival de Media Naranja / Media Vuelta') varies by school. Teacher must confirm the exact 3 sub-figures and whether Dile Que No happens after each part or only at the end.

name: Festival de Pelota
summary: A celebratory Rueda sequence that chains Pelota Una (1 clap), Pelota Dos (2 claps), and Pelota Tres (3 claps) back-to-back before finishing with a partner change into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-3, clap once in the center on 7 (Pelota Una), and return/exchange or step into the next Enchufla.
Execute the second Enchufla on 1-3 and clap twice rhythmically on 7-8 (Pelota Dos).
Execute the third Enchufla on 1-3 and clap three times (7-and-8) for Pelota Tres while traveling to the next follower.
Collect the new follower on 1-3 and complete Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn through the first Enchufla on 1-3 and clap once on 7 (Pelota Una).
Complete the second Enchufla turn on 1-3 and clap twice on 7-8 (Pelota Dos).
Complete the third Enchufla turn on 1-3 and clap three times on 7-and-8 (Pelota Tres) while holding your place on the circle.
Connect with the incoming leader on 1-3 and walk through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: Losing track of whether you are on 1, 2, or 3 claps.
Switching partners after every single Pelota instead of waiting for the end of the Festival sequence (or vice versa, depending on house rules).
Rushing the three claps on Pelota Tres.
variations: Switching partners after each individual Pelota (Una, Dos, Tres) over 6 eight-counts.
notes: UNSURE: Schools differ on whether 'Festival de Pelota' switches partners after each Pelota (1, 2, 3) or stays with the same partner until Pelota Tres. Teacher should confirm BOH Studios' house rule.

name: Festival de Pelota con Vuelta
summary: A celebratory sequence combining Pelota Una, Pelota Dos, and Pelota Tres in succession, adding a solo turn ('con vuelta') after each clap sequence and changing partners along the Rueda.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, clap once on 4 ('Pelota una'), and execute a solo turn on 5-6-7 while advancing to the next follower (or preparing Dile Que No).
Lead the new partner through Dile Que No on 1-2-3 and 5-6-7 (counts 9-16) to set up the second part.
On counts 17-24, lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, clap twice ('Pelota dos'), and execute a solo turn on 5-6-7 while advancing to the next follower.
Complete Dile Que No with the second new partner on counts 25-32.
On counts 33-40, lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, clap three times ('Pelota tres'), and turn on 5-6-7 toward the third follower.
Finish the festival with a clean Dile Que No on counts 41-48.

followerSteps.text: Turn in the Enchufla on 1-2-3, clap once on 4, and execute a solo turn in place on 5-6-7.
Dance Dile Que No with the arriving leader on counts 9-16.
On counts 17-24, turn in the Enchufla on 1-2-3, clap twice, and execute a solo turn in place on 5-6-7.
Dance Dile Que No with the second arriving leader on counts 25-32.
On counts 33-40, turn in the Enchufla on 1-2-3, clap three times, and execute a solo turn in place on 5-6-7.
Complete the final Dile Que No on counts 41-48.

commonMistakes: Losing count of which Pelota (1, 2, or 3 claps) the group is currently on.
Letting the solo turn pull the dancer off balance so they miss the Dile Que No connection.
Adding an extra Guapea between sections when the school runs the festival back-to-back.
variations: Compact 4-eight-count version where Pelota 1 and 2 happen without intermediate Dile Que Nos, finishing with Dile Que No only after Pelota 3.
notes: UNSURE: Some schools condense 'Festival de Pelota' so that the partner change and Dile Que No happen only at the very end, while others change partners on every Pelota (1, 2, and 3). Verify exact total eight-counts with the instructor.

name: Flor
summary: The 'Flower': a group Rueda formation call where all couples step inward toward the center on counts 1-3 raising their joined arms like blooming petals, then open outward on 5-7 and resolve into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: From open hold or Enchufla, step inward toward the center of the Rueda on 1-2-3 while raising your connected arms high toward the middle of the circle.
Step back outward toward the perimeter on 5-6-7, lowering and opening the arms like a blooming flower while shifting to the next follower.
Collect the follower in semi-closed frame on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step inward toward the center alongside the leader on 1-2-3, raising your arms smoothly toward the center point.
Open back out to the perimeter on 5-6-7 with graceful arm styling.
Step back on 9-11 and travel cleanly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Crowding the center too tightly and bumping hands or elbows with adjacent couples.
Dropping the arms abruptly instead of floating them down on counts 5-7.
variations: Flor staying with the original partner vs. Flor switching to the next partner on count 9.
notes: UNSURE: In some Rueda schools, 'La Flor' is a 1-bar styling flourish during Vamos Abajo/Al Centro rather than an Enchufla variation. Teacher should verify BOH Studios' version.

name: Fly
summary: A baseball-inspired Rueda partner-change call ('catching a fly ball'): during Dame or Enchufla, everyone claps once high above their head as if catching a baseball before picking up the next partner in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Open from Guapea (or Enchufla) on 1-2 and clap both hands high overhead on count 3 while looking up as if catching a fly ball, traveling toward the next follower.
Connect with the new follower in semi-closed frame on 5 and lead Dile Que No on 5-6-7.

followerSteps.text: Step 1-2-3 in place on the outer circle, executing the high overhead 'fly ball' clap on count 3.
Receive the new leader on 5 and travel cleanly through Dile Que No on 5-6-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Clapping wide to the side and accidentally striking a neighboring dancer's face; clap directly above your own forehead.
Stopping your footwork to look up at the ceiling on count 3.
variations: Enchufla con Fly (executing Enchufla on 1-3, high clap on 7, and Dile Que No on the second eight-count).
notes: Cuban Rueda vocabulary borrows heavily from baseball (Pelota, Fly, Doble Play, Triple Play, Rolling).

name: Foto
summary: A playful Rueda call where the leader and follower exchange places via Enchufla, strike a frozen camera-pose ('¡Foto!') together on counts 5-7, and then switch partners into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead a standard Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Step beside your partner (or frame them) on 5 and freeze completely in a playful photo pose through 6-7.
Release the pose on 9, travel to the next follower on 9-11, and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Complete the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Hit a fun, expressive freeze pose with your leader on 5-6-7 facing the center or an imaginary camera.
Step back on 9-11 to meet the incoming leader and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Jumping onto your partner or forcing an unled dip during the photo pose; keep both feet supported on the floor.
Breaking the freeze too early on count 6.
Forgetting whether the call stays with the same partner or switches on count 9.
variations: Foto con la Otra (striking the photo pose with the new partner on arrival).
notes: UNSURE: Check if BOH Studios switches partners after 'Foto' or returns to the same partner via Dile Que No.

name: Freezing on a Band Break
summary: Musicality drill where both partners arrest all momentum instantaneously on a sudden musical break (corte/bloque), hold stillness with active frame tension, and resume smoothly on beat 1.

leaderSteps.text: Anticipate the musical break on count 1 (or count 4/5 depending on the song's arrangement) by absorbing momentum into a grounded, bent-knee stance and signalling a gentle, unmistakable compression through the frame without yanking the follower's arms.

Hold the freeze or fill the silent space with subtle thoracic breath/attitude while keeping weight clearly committed to one foot, then prep the frame on count 8 to step cleanly back into timing on the next beat 1.

followerSteps.text: Match the leader's frame compression and the musical hit by settling weight completely over the standing foot, engaging the core to stop rotational or travelling momentum immediately.

Maintain poise and active frame connection during the hold (adding subtle shoulder or head styling if appropriate without shifting the feet), staying ready to feel which foot the leader initiates on count 1.

commonMistakes: Safety: Leaders forcibly pulling or jerking the follower's arms or shoulders to force a stop, which can strain wrists or rotator cuffs—the stop must come from core deceleration and clear chest-frame resistance.
Freezing with weight split 50/50 between both feet, leaving neither partner sure which foot is free to step on count 1.
Rushing back into the step on count 7 or 8 before the band actually drops back into the groove on 1.
variations: Adding a slow thoracic isolation or tembleque during the silent hold before locking back into the 1.
Breaking partner hold completely on the hit to strike complementary solo poses.
notes: In Timba, breaks (efectos/bloques) often happen on count 1, count 4, or count 8-and-1. Practice freezing on both odd and even phrases so students always know which foot is free when the rhythm resumes.

name: Hombres Derecha y Mujeres Izquierda
summary: A Rueda call where leaders and followers release into concentric circles or weave past each other—leaders travelling counter-clockwise (to their right) and followers travelling clockwise (to their left)—before reconnecting with a new partner via Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Execute an Enchufla or open release on 1-2-3 to face the center, then travel counter-clockwise (to the right) around the inside of the circle on 5-6-7, passing one or more followers moving in the opposite direction.
Pick up the designated follower on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and lead her through a Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15) to restore the Rueda.

followerSteps.text: Complete the opening Enchufla or release on 1-2-3, then travel clockwise (to the left along the outside track) on 5-6-7 while leaders move in the opposite direction on the inside.
Connect with the incoming leader on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) and step through a standard Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Leaders and followers travelling in the same lane instead of keeping leaders on the inner ring and followers on the outer ring, causing collisions.
Losing the 1-2-3, 5-6-7 stepping cadence and breaking into an unstructured jog around the circle.
Grabbing a partner abruptly while both people are moving in opposite directions—decelerate on counts 9-11 before leading Dile Que No.
variations: Weaving in and out (cadena/slalom style) as leaders and followers pass each other.
notes: UNSURE: Different Rueda groups use this call either for a 2-count opposite-direction pass (resulting in advancing two partners) or a continuous walking groove until the caller shouts 'Con la que te toque, Dile Que No'. Verify how many partners are skipped in your class.

name: Hombros (Shoulder Movement & Shimmy)
summary: Foundational Cuban upper-body isolation teaching dancers to roll, alternate, and shimmy the shoulders from the thoracic ribcage without tensing the neck or losing the footwork pulse.

leaderSteps.text: While stepping a compact basic (or in a grounded stance), alternate forward-and-back shoulder rolls on 1-2-3 driven by slight thoracic ribcage rotation.
Execute a double-time shoulder shimmy on 5-and-6-and-7 while keeping the traps and neck completely relaxed and eyes level.

followerSteps.text: Step compactly on 1-2-3 while rolling right and left shoulders in fluid alternation from the upper back.
Release into a fast, relaxed shoulder shimmy on 5-6-7 while maintaining grounded knees and natural hip sway.

commonMistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears (which creates tension) instead of moving them forward and back on a horizontal plane.
Flapping the elbows wide instead of isolating the shoulder girdle and ribcage.
Stopping the feet when the shoulders start moving.
variations: Combining single-time shoulder rolls (1-3) with double-time shimmies (5-7).
notes: Key biomechanical cue: initiate the movement from the ribcage and shoulder blades (scapulae), not by flapping the hands.

name: Indeciso
summary: The 'Indecisive Leader': after an Enchufla on 1-3, the leader alternates feints between the next follower on his right and his original follower on his left across counts 5-15 before finally committing to a partner for Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-3, then step toward the next follower on your right on 5-7 as if taking her.
Pivot back toward your original follower on 1-3 ('indecisive'), then pivot again on 5-7 toward the final target follower per house rule.
Connect cleanly on 1-3 and lead Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-3 and hold your perimeter station on 5-7.
Maintain a playful basic on the perimeter on 1-3 and 5-7 as the leaders feint left and right.
Connect with the leader who commits to your station on 1-3 and walk through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Leaders whipping their head and torso back and forth without spotting neighboring leaders.
Forgetting whether 'Indeciso' ends with the new partner or original partner in your school's syllabus.
variations: 2-bar fast Indeciso.
notes: UNSURE: Confirm whether BOH Studios finishes 'El Indeciso' with the next follower on the right or back with the original follower.

name: Isaura
summary: Named after the Brazilian telenovela Escrava Isaura, a huge hit in Cuba: an intermediate two-hand figure where the follower's wrists cross loosely in front before unwrapping into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: From a two-hand hold, lead an initial turn on 1-3 that crosses and wraps the follower's wrists together in front of her (or behind her back in a double hammerlock) on 5-7.
Walk or pivot together in the 'Isaura' crossed-wrist frame on 1-3, then raise the arms overhead on 5-7 to unlock the wrap.
Open into semi-closed hold on 1-3 and finish with Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn cleanly on 1-3 into the two-hand wrap on 5-7, keeping your wrists and elbows completely soft and relaxed.
Step compactly with the leader on 1-3 and unwind under the raised arms on 5-7.
Step back on 1-3 and walk through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Pulling or twisting the follower's crossed wrists; both dancers must use a frictionless two-finger hook grip with zero thumb clamping.
Standing too far apart during the wrap.
variations: Isaura con Dame (changing partners on the final Dile Que No).
notes: UNSURE: The telenovela *La Esclava Isaura* was a massive cultural phenomenon in Cuba; check with Enrique which exact wrist-wrap variation BOH Studios teaches under this name.

name: Juana la Cubana
summary: A lively, crowd-favourite Casino and Rueda combination featuring an Enchufla-style entry, an overhead lasso/hook wrap, and a playful rhythmic walk or hip accent before Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla or Setenta entry on 1-3, catching the follower in a two-hand or shoulder-level wrap on 5-7.
Guide the follower through a circular promenade or playful rhythmic check on 1-3 and 5-7, emphasizing the upbeat Timba groove.
Unwrap the follower with a clean overhead turn on 1-3 and finish with Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Execute the entry turn on 1-3 and settle into the wrap on 5-7 with soft knees and active frame.
Match the leader's rhythmic walks and hip accents on 1-3 and 5-7 with joyful Cuban styling.
Unwind under the raised arm on 1-3 and complete Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Rushing the overhead unwrap and clipping the partner's head or hair.
Dancing the middle section flat without musical expression.
Losing the count during the playful check.
variations: In Rueda de Casino, adding a vocal shout or clap on the break before switching partners.
notes: UNSURE: Named after the famous Fito Olivares / Cuban party track; different academies teach distinct 2- or 3-eight-count sequences under this name. Teacher must verify BOH Studios' exact counts.

name: La Familia
summary: A warm community Rueda call where an Enchufla brings the group together toward the center for a group embrace or family pose before leaders pick up the next follower into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 to bring yourself toward the inside of the circle.
Step in on 5-6-7 to link arms/shoulders with neighboring dancers (or your current and next follower) in a joyful 'Familia' huddle.
Release on 9, pick up the next follower on your right on 9-11, and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn left through the Enchufla on 1-2-3.
Step slightly inward on 5-6-7 to join the warm 'Familia' group connection and smile across the circle.
Open back to the perimeter on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No with the new leader on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Pulling neighboring dancers by the neck during the group huddle; rest hands lightly on upper shoulders/backs.
Taking too long to release the huddle and missing count 9.
variations: Combining Prima, Prima con la Hermana, and La Familia in a 3-call storytelling sequence.
notes: UNSURE: Some schools teach 'La Familia' as the 3rd part of 'Prima -> Prima con la Hermana -> Con toda la Familia'. Teacher should confirm BOH Studios' sequence.

name: La Prima Cruzada
summary: A crossed-hand or cross-circle variation of Prima (Adiós) where the leader executes the Prima duck-under with a two-hand crossed connection (or crosses the circle) before resolving into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Take a crossed two-hand hold (or initiate Prima) on 1-2-3, stepping across in front of the follower while passing under the raised top arm.
Unwind or exchange places on 5-6-7 while keeping the lower hand soft at waist level.
Open the frame on 9-11 and complete Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step forward/in-place on 1-2-3 as the leader passes across in front of you under the raised arm.
Pivot smoothly through the crossed-hand unwind on 5-6-7 with soft elbows.
Step back on 9-11 and walk cleanly through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Ducking with a rounded back or bent neck instead of lowering with the knees.
Raising the wrong hand of the cross on count 1, locking the wrists.
variations: La Prima Cruzada switching to the next partner.
notes: UNSURE: Confirm whether BOH Studios teaches 'La Prima Cruzada' as a two-hand crossed Prima or a Prima that crosses the center of the Rueda.

name: El Lazo
summary: The 'Lasso': a smooth figure where the leader loops the connected arm over the follower's head and shoulders like a lasso before gliding around the circle and releasing into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: From open hold, step 1-2-3 while raising the joined right (or two-hand) connection to loop cleanly over the follower's head onto their shoulder level.
Circle clockwise around the follower on 5-6-7, guiding them with a gentle lasso frame at shoulder/upper-back height.
Lift the lasso loop back up and over on 9-11 to release the wrap, finishing with Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Step in place/Guapea on 1-2-3 while keeping your head upright as the leader loops the arm overhead.
Pivot and walk smoothly around the shared axis on 5-6-7, feeling the gentle circular guidance from the looped arm.
Turn cleanly out of the loop on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Dropping the lasso loop onto the follower's neck or throat; the arm must rest lightly at shoulder/scapula level or clear the head completely.
Making the overhead loop too small, forcing the follower to duck.
Pulling with the arm instead of stepping around the circle.
variations: Lazo Doble (looping first the follower, then the leader).
notes: Emphasize neck safety in class: the overhead loop should float with zero downward pressure on the neck.

name: Mambo Adelante y Atrás
summary: The classic forward-and-back solo Mambo basic used in Suelta shines and Rueda breaks, emphasizing grounded weight checks and Cuban hip pendulum.

leaderSteps.text: Step left foot forward on 1, rock weight back onto right foot in place on 2, and bring left foot back underneath your hip on 3.
Step right foot backward on 5, rock weight forward onto left foot in place on 6, and close right foot underneath your hip on 7.

followerSteps.text: Step right foot backward on 1 (or left foot forward in solo line-up), transfer weight in place on 2, and collect underneath your hip on 3.
Step the opposite foot forward/back on 5, rock weight in place on 6, and collect on 7 with natural Cuban hip motion.

commonMistakes: Taking giant forward lunges on count 1 instead of keeping the step compact under the torso.
Failing to transfer 100% of body weight onto the standing foot on counts 2 and 6.
Stiffening the ankles and heels.
variations: Adding a subtle tap or brush in the middle on counts 4 and 8.
notes: In solo Suelta warmups, everyone typically starts with the left foot forward on 1; inside partnerwork or Rueda, followers mirror on the right foot.

name: Media Doble
summary: An intermediate Rueda partner-change figure that doubles the check/turn action of Una Media before advancing to the next follower for Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla entry on 1-2-3.
Execute the double half-turn check or double arm-hook exchange on 5-6-7 while moving along the inside of the circle.
Connect with the next follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Follow the double check/turn sequence on 5-6-7 on the outer perimeter.
Receive the incoming leader on 9-11 and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Rushing the double check and losing the 5-6-7 footwork rhythm.
Pulling the partner off her spot.
variations: Media Triple (Advanced 3-bar version).
notes: Prerequisite for 'Media Triple' in Batch 13.

name: Media Triple
summary: The advanced triple-phrase extension of Una Media and Media Doble, chaining three consecutive half-turn checks or multi-partner passes before resolving into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead the Enchufla entry on 1-3 and execute the first half-turn/hook check on 5-7.
Execute the second check on 1-3 and the third check/turn on 5-7 while advancing along the circle.
Collect the incoming follower on 1-3 and finish with Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn through the Enchufla on 1-3 and match the first check on 5-7.
Execute the second and third rhythmic checks/turns on 1-3 and 5-7 on the perimeter.
Connect with the leader on 1-3 and walk cleanly through Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: Losing count of the three checks and starting Dile Que No a bar early.
Tensing the arms.
variations: Media Triple progressing past three followers.
notes: Completes the Una Media -> Media Doble -> Media Triple progression.

name: ¡Mentira!
summary: 'Lie / Fake-out!': called mid-Dame or mid-Enchufla—the leader fakes moving to the next follower on counts 1-3, then pivots back on the '¡Mentira!' shout to keep their original partner in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Start a Dame or Enchufla partner change on 1-3, stepping toward the next follower on your right.
When the caller shouts '¡Mentira!', check your forward momentum on 5, pivot 180 degrees on 6-7, and return to your original follower.
Pick up your original follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute your 1-2-3 entry as if changing partners.
On the '¡Mentira!' call, keep your visual focus on your original leader as he pivots back toward you on 5-6-7.
Reconnect with your original leader on 9-11 and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Leaders stopping dead and backing up blindly without looking; always pivot cleanly on the ball of your foot.
Ignoring the '¡Mentira!' call and colliding with the leader who stayed with his partner.
variations: Dame con Mentira (1-eight-count quick fake on 1-2, return on 3, Dile Que No on 5-7).
notes: Does NOT change partner—its whole purpose is cancelling an in-progress partner change!

name: Mujeres al Centro
summary: 'Followers to the Center!': after an Enchufla or open prep, all followers step into the center of the Rueda on counts 1-7 to dance solo shines or a group groove while leaders clap on the outside perimeter, before re-pairing in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla (or open release) on 1-2-3 that sends the follower inward toward the center of the circle while you step to the outer perimeter.
Hold the outer perimeter on 5-6-7, clapping the clave/tumbao rhythm and cheering the followers in the middle as you shift toward the next follower.
Step in on 9-11 to collect the follower (or next follower) and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Turn inward on 1-2-3 to form a tight inner circle with all the other followers in the center of the Rueda.
Dance expressive solo shines, hip isolations, or a synchronized clap in the center on 5-6-7.
Open back out to the perimeter on 9-11 to connect with the leader and walk through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Followers backing out of the center blindly on count 9; look over your shoulder as you return to the perimeter.
Leaders forgetting to keep the outer circle evenly spaced while clapping.
variations: Keeping followers in the center for 2 or 3 full eight-counts during a Timba despelote section until the caller shouts 'Dile Que No'.
notes: One of the best calls for highlighting the followers during a musical breakdown.

name: Mujeres Derecha, Mujeres Izquierda
summary: A Rueda call where leaders hold the circle stations while followers travel first to the right (counter-clockwise) on the first eight-count and then reverse to the left (clockwise) on the second eight-count, finishing with Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3 to send the current follower to the right (counter-clockwise), then stay in place marking time on 5-6-7 while receiving and passing the incoming follower.
Redirect the follower back to the left (clockwise) on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), catch the returning partner, and lead her through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Turn under the leader's arm on 1-2-3 and travel to the right (counter-clockwise) around the circle on 5-6-7 to the adjacent leader.
Pivot and reverse direction to the left (clockwise) on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), returning to the previous leader (or next designated leader), and complete Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Leaders travelling around the circle when only the followers ('mujeres') are called to move.
Followers overturning on the direction change at count 8/9 and losing balance.
Leaders pulling the follower's arm to reverse her trajectory instead of offering a clear open-palm check.
variations: Ending on a different partner if the caller extends one direction longer than the other.
notes: UNSURE: Confirm whether the follower returns to her original partner (net zero partner change) or advances one partner depending on whether 'derecha' starts from an Enchufla swap. Add or remove 'partner-change' tag during teacher review if needed.

name: Ni Pa' Ti Ni Pa' Mí
spanishName: Ni pa' ti ni pa' mí
summary: 'Neither for you nor for me': after an Enchufla, the leader claps/skips the immediate follower on the right ('not for me, not for you') and travels to the second follower into Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, exchanging places with your current follower.
Pass by the first follower on your right on 5-6-7 while gesturing or clapping ('ni pa' ti, ni pa' mí'), continuing anticlockwise toward the next follower.
Arrive in front of the second follower on 9-11 and lead Dile Que No on 13-15.

followerSteps.text: Execute the Enchufla left turn on 1-2-3.
Hold your place on the outer circle on 5-6-7, clapping or wagging a playful finger as the first leader passes you by.
Connect with the second incoming leader on 9-11 and travel through Dile Que No on 13-15.

commonMistakes: Stopping at the first follower instead of skipping her.
Followers stepping into the inside lane while leaders are passing two spots.
variations: Shouting '¡Ni pa' ti, ni pa' mí!' in unison with the Rueda on counts 5-7.
notes: UNSURE: Some schools execute 'Ni pa' ti ni pa' mí' as a double-clap in the center between two leaders before taking the second partner. Teacher should confirm BOH Studios' version.

name: Ni Pa' Ti Ni Pa' Mí con Vuelta
spanishName: Ni Pa' Ti Ni Pa' Mí con Vuelta
summary: A playful Rueda partner-change figure where the leader leads an Enchufla, claps and wags a finger ('neither for you nor for me!') while skipping past the immediate follower with a solo turn ('con vuelta'), and picks up the next partner in Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Lead an Enchufla on 1-2-3, release the current follower, and on 5-6-7 gesture/clap toward her and the next follower ('ni pa' ti, ni pa' mí').
Execute a solo 360-degree turn on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11) while travelling past to the designated new partner, and lead her through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

followerSteps.text: Turn left in the Enchufla on 1-2-3, then mark basic steps in place on 5-6-7 while performing the playful 'ni pa' ti, ni pa' mí' clap/gesture.
Execute a solo 360-degree turn in place on 1-2-3 (counts 9-11), connect with the arriving leader on count 12, and travel through Dile Que No on 5-6-7 (counts 13-15).

commonMistakes: Stopping with the first follower instead of advancing to the correct partner.
Losing the 1-2-3 timing during the solo spin on counts 9-11.
Forgetting the playful attitude and eye contact that give the call its name.
variations: Performing a double clap before the finger wag on counts 5-7.
notes: UNSURE: Confirm whether the leader skips one follower (like Dame Dos) or advances to the immediate next follower after teasing both.

name: Obatalá (Orisha of Peace, Wisdom & Purity)
summary: Sacred dance vocabulary of Obatalá, the creator of human bodies and father and elder of the Orishas representing purity, clarity of mind, and peace—danced in immaculate white with either calm, trembling-elder paths or proud warrior paths.

leaderSteps.text: In the elder path (caminos viejos): incline the upper back slightly forward with knees bent, stepping slowly and deliberately on 1-3 and 5-7 while gently sweeping the iruke (white horsetail whisk) to bless and bring peace.
Allow a subtle, dignified tremor in the shoulders and hands on 1-3 and 5-7 (or in warrior paths like Ayáguna, rise upright with proud, slashing sword gestures).

followerSteps.text: Adopt the serene, bowed posture of the elder Obatalá on 1-3 and 5-7, taking grounded, measured steps while cleansing the space with gentle white-iruke wrist sweeps.
Maintain deep internal focus and rhythmic shoulder/torso articulation on 1-3 and 5-7, embodying wisdom and tranquility.

commonMistakes: Treating the bowed elder posture as comedic or weak; Obatalá's movement must radiate immense dignity, authority, and serenity.
Rushing the slow, weighted steps.
variations: Contrasting the calm elder path of Obatalá with the energetic warrior path of Obatalá Ayáguna.
notes: Sacred in Regla de Ocha: Obatalá's colour is pure white (and silver); his number is 8, and his attribute is the white iruke and silver agogó bell. Never present the elder paths as parody.

name: Ochenta (80)
summary: A classic intermediate knot figure building on Setenta (70), featuring a double-hand wrap where both leader and follower execute sequential overhead unwraps and hammerlock switches.

leaderSteps.text: Begin with a Setenta entry on 1-3 into the follower's hammerlock, and exchange places on 5-7 while keeping both hands connected.
Instead of releasing, turn inward under the raised left arm on 1-3 so both partners share the wrap, then lead the follower's overhead turn on 5-7.
Unwind the final arm knot on 1-3 and lead a clean Dile Que No on 5-7.

followerSteps.text: Turn right into the Setenta hammerlock on 1-3 and travel across on 5-7 with a soft right elbow.
Maintain small steps on 1-3 as the leader turns into the wrap, then pivot under the raised arm on 5-7.
Step out of the unwrap on 1-3 and complete Dile Que No on 5-7.

commonMistakes: SAFETY: Over-rotating the shoulder in the double hammerlock; both dancers must take tiny steps close to each other so arms never pull taut.
Gripping with thumbs during the knot transitions.
Rushing the final unwrap before count 1.
variations: Ochenta Complicado (adding a Siete check before the final exit).
notes: UNSURE: As with 84 and 88, exact count-by-count hand switches for Ochenta (80) vary slightly by school. Verify with Enrique.

name: Ochenta y Cuatro (84)
summary: A classic numbered Casino figure belonging to the Setenta family that combines a two-hand hammerlock entry with an overhead unwrap and directional turn reversal before Dile Que No.

leaderSteps.text: Enter with a two-hand hold as in Setenta: step 1-2-3 turning the follower right into a hammerlock wrap, then walk around on 5-6-7 to face the follower.
